questions.question: ‘Akbar Nama’ is a ______-volume history of Akbar’s reign, written by Abul Fazl.
questions.solution:
The 'Akbar Nama' is a three-volume work by Abul Fazl.
  • The third volume is the famous 'Ain-i-Akbari'.

questions.question: ______ fought for the rights of the Dalit community.
questions.solution:
Bhimrao Ambedkar is the chief architect of the Indian Constitution and a champion of Dalit rights.
  • He founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha.

questions.question: Who established the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON)?
questions.solution:
A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada founded ISKCON in 1966 in New York City.
  • It is based on the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers did NOT belong to the Mauryan Dynasty?
questions.solution:
Bimbisara belonged to the Haryanka Dynasty, not the Mauryan Dynasty.
  • Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya and the father of Ashoka.

questions.question: Which state of India was ruled by the Ningthouja dynasty?
questions.solution:
The Ningthouja Dynasty ruled the Manipur Kingdom for nearly 2,000 years.
  • It is one of the longest-running dynasties in the world.

questions.question: Gautamiputra Satakarni was the greatest ruler of the ______ Empire in the 2nd century CE.
questions.solution:
Gautamiputra Satakarni was the most powerful ruler of the Satavahana Dynasty.
  • He is described as the 'Ekabrahmana' and the destroyer of Shakas.

questions.question: 'Banabhatta', well known for his literary works, flourished during the reign of ______.
questions.solution:
Banabhatta was the court poet of Harshavardhana.
  • His works provide deep insight into the 7th-century administration.

questions.question: King Shashanka, against whom Harshvardhana declared war, was a ruler of the ______ kingdom.
questions.solution:
King Shashanka was the ruler of Gauda (Bengal).
  • He was a contemporary and rival of Harshavardhana.
  • He is said to have cut down the Bodhi Tree at Bodh Gaya.

questions.question: Who among the following Indian revolutionaries conceived an armed insurrection against the British in cooperation with Germany?
questions.solution:
Bagha Jatin (Jatin Mukherjee) planned an armed insurrection with German help during WWI (The Zimmermann Plan).
  • He died after a heroic gunfight with the British at Balasore.

questions.question: In which of the following regions did Baba Ramchandra mainly lead the peasant struggle during colonial rule?
questions.solution:
Baba Ramchandra led the peasant struggle in the Awadh region of Uttar Pradesh.
  • He used to recite the Ramayana to mobilize the rural masses.

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest of the Vedas?
questions.solution:
The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas (dated approx. 1500–1000 BC).
  • It contains 1,028 hymns (Suktas).

questions.question: Who was the first Mughal emperor?
questions.solution:
Babur was the founder and first emperor of the Mughal Dynasty.
  • He wrote his autobiography 'Baburnama' in Chaghatai Turkic.

questions.question: In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi organised a satyagraha for the peasants of Kheda district of Gujarat. The satyagraha was for the demand of:
questions.solution:
The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) was for revenue relaxation due to crop failure and plague.
  • It was Gandhiji's first non-cooperation movement.

questions.question: When did the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly take place?
questions.solution:
The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on 9 December 1946.
  • Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the interim president.

questions.question: In 1862, the High Court was first established at:
questions.solution:
In 1862, High Courts were established in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras.
  • The High Courts Act was passed in 1861.

questions.question: Which of the following was built by Muhammed Quli Qutub Shah?
questions.solution:
Muhammed Quli Qutub Shah built the Charminar in 1591 to commemorate the end of a plague.
  • He was the founder of the city of Hyderabad.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784?
questions.solution:
William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784 to promote Oriental studies.
  • Warren Hastings was the Governor-General at the time.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in:
questions.solution:
Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915.
  • This day is celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.question: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 at:
questions.solution:
The Indian National Congress (INC) was founded in 1885 at Bombay.
  • The first session was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Arya Samaj in 1875?
questions.solution:
Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875.
  • He gave the slogan 'Go back to the Vedas'.
  • He wrote 'Satyarth Prakash'.

questions.question: 'Rang Ghar', one of Asia's oldest amphitheatres, was built by the king of the ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
Rang Ghar is an 18th-century amphitheater built by Ahom King Pramatta Singha in Assam.
  • It is located in Sivasagar.

questions.question: The first English factory was set up on the banks of the river ______ in 1651.
questions.solution:
The first English factory was established on the banks of the Hugli River in Bengal in 1651.
  • This was done during the reign of Shah Jahan.

questions.question: In which year was the Communist Party of India - Marxist (CPI-M) formed?
questions.solution:
The Communist Party of India (Marxist) or CPI-M was formed in 1964 following a split in the CPI.
  • It was led by leaders like E.M.S. Namboodiripad.

questions.question: The ancient city of Hampi was the capital of the ______ empire.
questions.solution:
Hampi was the capital of the Vijayanagar Empire (founded 1336).
  • It is located on the banks of the Tungabhadra River in Karnataka.

questions.question: During the reign of which of the following Sultans of Delhi was actual power enjoyed by Balban?
questions.solution:
Balban exercised actual power as the Naib (deputy) to Sultan Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah.
  • He later became the Sultan and introduced the policy of 'Blood and Iron'.
